tagsub: EP. 12 · INDIA V NEW ZEALAND ODI SERIES
sources: Ball-by-ball for the four matches played: Cricbuzz full-commentary captures (1st: match 161245, 2nd: 161256, 4th: 161271, 5th: 161282), parsed into one row per delivery (data/series/nz_ind_2026). Totals, individual figures and the series leaders (Young 162, Kohli 86, Brar 9 wkts, Duffy 9 wkts) checked against Wikipedia's 'Indian cricket team in New Zealand in 2026-27' (citing Cricinfo): 26 validation checks; the 4th ODI also agrees with an independent Cricinfo capture over by over.
The 3rd ODI (Hamilton, 10 November) had no play. The 1st ODI was decided by DLS (target 143 from 32 overs) and the 2nd on DLS (India 113/7, 4 runs ahead of the par score of 109).

Win probability added: our own model, fitted on 1,719 men's 50-over ODIs in the Cricsheet archive (2009 onwards, no rain method); an indication, not a fact (matches 1 and 2 were rain-affected). Drops: the runs a batter scored after the first dropped chance (descriptive, not a counterfactual); Cricbuzz's own note during the 5th ODI also puts India's drops at eight. Figures: analysis/nz_ind_*.py, make_nz_ind_series.py.

long.vo: Eight dropped catches in four matches. And India still won the one-day series, three-one. How? We went through every ball.

scene.kicker: INDIA V NEW ZEALAND · ODI SERIES 2026
scene.title: Eight dropped catches.
scene.label: India's let-offs across the four matches played · the series finished 3-1 to India (one washout)

long.vo: This is a Data Story: the whole series, from our own ball-by-ball data for every match that was played.

scene.teaser: ODI series · November 2026 · four matches played, one washed out

long.vo: Four results. Won by five wickets in Auckland. Won by four runs in Wellington. Hamilton, washed out. Lost by two hundred and forty-four runs at Bay Oval. Then won by twenty-two runs, at the same ground, two days later.

scene.kicker: THE FOUR RESULTS · INDIA'S SCORE v NEW ZEALAND'S
scene.title: Win, win, wash-out, loss, win.

long.vo: Two of the three wins came under the rain rules. In Auckland, the target was cut to one forty-three from thirty-two overs. In Wellington, play stopped at one thirteen for seven, four runs ahead of the par score.

India bowled New Zealand out in all four innings. But look at the averages. India's attack took thirty-seven wickets at twenty-two point three. New Zealand's took thirty-two, at seventeen point two. The fourth match explains it: without it, India's bowlers average seventeen point three, and New Zealand's twenty-one.

scene.title: Bowled out four times. Worse average.

long.vo: The top order was the other problem. India's third wicket fell at one twenty-four, thirty-nine, nought, and thirty-four. In the fourth match, India were nought for three.

scene.kicker: INDIA'S SCORE WHEN THE THIRD WICKET FELL
scene.title: Three down, early.

long.vo: विराट कोहली, India's top scorer in the series, made seventy-four in Auckland, then seven, nought, and five. Eighty-six runs in total, from four innings.

scene.title: 86 runs. 74 of them in one game.

long.vo: And the catching. India dropped eight chances in the four matches, and New Zealand four. The batters let off first scored two hundred and forty-four more runs after India's drops, and ninety-six after New Zealand's. Will Young, dropped twice in two balls in the fourth match, went on to score a hundred and twenty after the first.

scene.title: Eight drops. 244 runs.
rows: Runs by the let-off batters afterwards

long.vo: The leading run-scorers: Will Young, a hundred and sixty-two. Then Tim Seifert, a hundred and ten. Then विराट कोहली, with eighty-six. For the bowlers, गुरनूर बराड़ and Jacob Duffy took nine wickets each.
By our win-probability measure, the most valuable player of the series was अर्शदीप सिंह, then नमन धीर, अक्षर पटेल, and गुरनूर बराड़. The most costly: रोहित शर्मा.

scene.kicker: WIN PROBABILITY ADDED OVER THE SERIES · OUR MODEL
scene.title: Who really won it?

long.vo: Three grounds, three different games. New Zealand's first innings scored four point six an over in Auckland, three point three in Wellington, and six point seven at Bay Oval in the fourth match. India's first innings at Bay Oval, in the fifth, five an over.

So how did India win three-one? They bowled well, and they won two matches under the rain rules, and they escaped, in the fifth, by a margin smaller than their let-offs. The thing to fix is the catching.
Was this a series India deserved to win? Tell us in the comments, and follow for more Data Stories.

Every ball of the four matches played: the two DLS wins, the 244-run defeat at Bay Oval, the top order that kept falling early, India's catching (244 runs scored after India's drops against 96 after New Zealand's), the series leaders, and our win-probability ranking of who really won it.
